findings.reason: the section's single deliverable is naming the origin, and the instrument cannot observe the real completion (the receipts hold no response body), so its clearing rule can send §3's fix at the model when the parser is the cause.
findings.text: §2 tests each leaked call only by reconstructing a two-call completion that is always well-formed, while its own case list allows the leak to arise from the malformed shape "a second call that begins before the first call's argument closes"; a parser that leaks on the malformed shape but splits a well-formed completion is cleared by the per-call test, and §2 then names the model as the origin

findings.reason: the plan's whole §3 fix is selected by the origin §2 names, so an unsound discrimination routes the repair at the wrong layer.
findings.text: the done-when's clearing condition, "the completion splits into two calls, which leaves the model writing the token inside a string as the only way to the delivered argument", does not follow: a merge of the synthetic completion is equally consistent with the model having written the token in a single string, and a split is equally consistent with the parser failing on a shape the reconstruction never builds, so neither branch isolates one origin; the fig-01 argument re-read from `stream.jsonl` (`file_path` truncated to `...` and the second call's `<｜DSML｜ invoke name="Bash">`/`<｜DSML｜ parameter name="command">` markup absorbed into it) shows the leak arriving in a shape the reconstruction's assumption of two well-formed calls does not cover
